newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND PRODUCE MIXED PERFORMANCE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND PRODUCE MIXED PERFORMANCE.

text.p: England produced a statistically impressive yet curiously disjointed start to the Five Nations' championship on Saturday.

The defending champions overwhelmed Scotland by a record winning margin of 41-13 at Twickenham, scoring three tries in the space of five minutes after an hour of uninspiring and often indifferent rugby.
In the other second round match Ireland, unbeaten in their previous six visits to Cardiff, triumphed again, albeit by only one point, with a 26-25 victory over Wales.
England's first half performance was lacklustre and they were lucky to take a 16-10 lead into the interval after referee Paddy O'Brien awarded a penalty try for deliberate offside.
Scotland, beaten 34-19 by Wales in the first round, narrowed the margin to three points before their defence cracked in the face of some sustained pressure by the massive England forwards.

Scrum-half Andy Gomarsall capitalised on a burst by lock Martin Johnson, Will Carling, who had an outstanding game throughout, scored his first try against the Scots and Phil de Glanville, his successor as captain, scored the third.
"We put a lot of work in and at the end scored some tries and, as we are always hearing we don't score tries, that was very satisfying," Carling said.

De Glanville, who needed a good performance on Saturday to confirm his place in the side ahead of Jeremy Guscott, said: "We did what we needed to do in the first half and then gradually the opportunities and the space came in the second half and we made us of it."
England, though, still looked one-paced, lacked penetration for most of the match and the game generally was riddled with basic errors.

Scotland captain Rob Wainwright, whose chances of captaining the British Lions in South Africa this year seem to be slipping by the match, stated the obvious when he said: "Our defence just wasn't up to the mark really."
Ireland, who have lost each of their four matches at Lansdowne Road this season, appear to relish the trip across the Irish sea and the big-match atmosphere at the national stadium.
The Irish, who lost 32-15 to France in the opening round, ran up a 20-10 halftime lead through tries by Jonathan Bell, Eric Miller and new cap Dennis Hickie which ultimately proved decisive.

Ieuan Evans scored a try in each half, improving his national record to 33, while their impressive number eight Scott Quinnell, who also scored against Scotland, barged over late in the match to reduce the deficit to a point.
Ireland held on in a frantic final few minutes and, as Welsh skipper Jonathan Humphreys, commented: "We left it far too late."
Evans, sprightly as ever in his 33rd year, has still not played in a winning Wales' side against Ireland at home and talk of a Welsh revival will have to be put on hold for the time being.
"We let Ireland control the pattern of the game and they dominated us," Evans said. ""We've got to pick ourselves up afer this."
